title: HOOK//30 GROOVE (recognition, transformation, payoff)
description: HOOK//30 candidate A. The B1 hook over a 3+3+2 kick and backbeat; then the bass sings the hook half a beat late, a low second voice answers, they trade twos, four stop-time chords and a breath; then the hook returns and is answered a third higher, and the B1 mallet stretto becomes a conversation between bars and tines that speeds from eighths to triplets to sixteenths into the loop.

sections.development: B1 note for note in voice, bass, mallets and clock, now over a 3+3+2 kick (the bass riff's own rhythm) and a backbeat. Dm | Bb | Gm C | Dm A7

stop-time, half-time clock: the bass sings the hook a fifth lower and half a beat late; a low second voice answers; bass and lead trade the rising sixth in twos against the mallets' falling sixth; four syncopated chords on the hook's dotted rhythm, then silence and one breath. Gm7 | C9 | F Bb | Em7b5 Eb9

the hook with its own answer sung under it; then answered a third higher for the first time (the answer becomes the harmony); the mallet stretto split between bars and tines, speeding from eighths to triplets to sixteenths; the inverted cadence over a dominant pedal. Dm | F | Gm C | Dm/A A7

cues.label: the B1 hook (voice), over the 3+3+2 kick
the cry: the rising sixth lands on F5
B1 stretto: mallets play the rising sixth twice as fast against the voice
movement II: the bass sings the hook, half a beat late
bass and lead trade the rising sixth; mallets mirror it downwards
four stop-time chords on the hook's dotted rhythm (beats 28, 28.75, 29.5, 30.25)
the B1 pickup announces the hook
movement III: the hook returns with its answer sung under it
the hook answered a third higher for the first time
bars and tines trade the stretto in eighths while the voice reaches up
the trade speeds up: eighth triplets
sixteenths: the tines run, then the stretto at four times its first speed against the B1 pickup, ending on octave As
loop point: A7 resolves to the first bar
